newsitem.title: JAPAN: Hitachi to start making FRAM chips - paper.
newsitem.headline: Hitachi to start making FRAM chips - paper.

text.p: Hitachi Ltd will start commercial production of ferroelectric random-access memory (FRAM) chips by the end of March 1997 to lower the ratio of dynamic random access memory (DRAM) chips in its total semiconductor output, a Japanese newspaper said on Tuesday.

The industrial daily Nikkan Kogyo Shimbun said Hitachi would initially make 20,000 to 30,000 256 kilobit FRAMs a month, increasing the amount to 200,000 to 300,000 chips monthly by the end of calendar 1997.
The paper said Hitachi would also make one megabit and four megabit FRAMs.
Hitachi spokesmen were not immediately available for comment.
FRAM chips can retain memory without electricity and the memory can be rewritten up to one trillion times.
Prices of DRAM chips have been falling sharply due to excessive production by chip makers.
